translation: The Classic says, "The essence and splendor of the five viscera and six bowels all ascend and pour into the eye. The essence of the bones becomes the pupil, belonging to the kidneys. The essence of the sinews becomes the black orb, belonging to the liver. The essence of the blood becomes the network vessels, belonging to the heart. The essence of the qi becomes the white orb, belonging to the lungs. The essence of the flesh becomes the eyelids, belonging to the spleen. The channels of blood and qi are attached above to the brain and emerge behind at the nape. If one is affected by the six excesses from without, the seven emotions injuring within, loss of moderation in food and drink, or excess of toil and labor, all can damage the eye." Now the eye communicates with the orifice of the liver, and the kidneys store its essence. Once there is pent-up frustration, the ministerial fire rides the liver wood and ascends, and in the end the transformations become manifold, giving rise to the name of the seventy-two syndromes. In sum, they do not go beyond the two barriers of internal and external. Hua Yuanhua said, "The eye resembles a round object; the pupil spirit dwells in the center and faces forward, like the sun and moon that are bright in the southeast and dim in the northwest." There are the spirit ointment, the spirit water, and the spirit light; the true blood, the true qi, and the true essence—these are the source fluids that nourish the eye. The spirit ointment is the ointment contained within the eye; when the spirit declines, there is damage. The spirit water originates from the triple burner, being transformed from the true one qi of the prenatal; it is the water that moistens the surface of the eye. When the water declines, there is the affliction of fire prevailing and dryness and violence; when the water is exhausted, there is the disease of the eye orb being large or small; when it is depleted and astringent, there is the danger of dimness and blindness. Those who are deficient are many, and those who are full are few; for this reason the world has no eye of complete essence. The spirit light originates in the life gate, communicates with the gallbladder, and is emitted from the heart—it is the fire doing its work. When the fire declines, there is the affliction of dimness and darkness; when the fire blazes, there is the calamity of burning and dryness. Now the heart is the sovereign, communicating with the inner canthus; therefore what is greatly red is real fire. The life gate is the lesser heart; the lesser heart is the ministerial fire, which acts in place of the sovereign and communicates with the outer canthus; therefore what is slightly red in the outer canthus is deficient fire. If the sovereign remains still and silent, then the ministerial fire is naturally clear and tranquil. The true blood is the blood that ascends and moves within the liver to nourish the eye and pour into the network vessels. This blood is not like the blood that moves easily among the flesh; it is the water born of the heavenly one, and so it is called true. The true qi is the qi that comes and goes and moves and generates within the channels of the eye; it is the original yang that the true one of the prenatal generates. The true essence is the essence fluid transformed from the original qi of the two heavens, prenatal and postnatal; it arises in the kidneys, is dispensed to the gallbladder, and only then reaches the pupil spirit. If any one of these several things is damaged, the eye then becomes diseased. Wulüzi said, "The eye is born of the qi of the prenatal and formed by the qi of the postnatal; it is the subtle accumulation of yin and yang and the essence and splendor of water and fire. The blood nourishes the water, the water nourishes the ointment, the ointment protects the pupil spirit, the qi is the moving force, and the spirit is what maintains it. Compared to the sun and moon, the principle is truly the same. It is the greatest treasure of the human body and should be valued."
translator_notes: 約束 (yueshu) refers to the eyelids; the essence of the flesh forms the eyelids.
大眥 (dazi) and 小眥 (xiaozhi) refer to the inner and outer canthi respectively.
小心 (lesser heart) is another name for the life gate (mingmen).
無閭子 (Wulüzi) appears to be a personal name but cannot be confirmed.
